signal_series.self_check_contract: fred_vintage.assert_vintage_trustworthy(): HTTP 200 is NOT proof. Compares as-of vintage vs latest; resolves 'identical' into (a) revised->distinguishable, (b) single vintage date -> genuinely-never-revised (EVIDENCE, trustworthy), (c) identical despite many vintages -> endpoint served latest = the trap (NOT trustworthy, investigate); plus a known-revised positive control (GDPC1) that, if it also comes back identical, flags the point-in-time call itself as broken.
signal_series.expected_finding_once_key_available: BAMLH0A0HYM2 / BAA10YM are market-price-derived, so vintage is expected to ~equal latest. The self-check turns that into an evidence-backed conclusion (single/few vintage dates => not revised) rather than an unverified assumption — which is what §3's killer test actually needs for these series. If, instead, many vintages exist and vintage==latest, that is the trap and must be investigated before any verdict.
